operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL and mixed-case (Album, AlbumId, PlaylistTrack); generated SQL must double-quote original spelling.
No spaces in names; no dangling FKs; all parent tables/columns exist.
Self-FK Employee.ReportsTo -> Employee.EmployeeId: table self-edge must be ignored in table_order, column edge kept.
Composite PK PlaylistTrack(PlaylistId,TrackId) with both members also FKs to Playlist/Track; composite-PK members get max_l0=30.
Employee.ReportsTo has NULLs (0.125) and only 3 distinct values; FK draw from parent's final filtered EmployeeId list.
datetime columns (BirthDate, HireDate, InvoiceDate) store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; declared type 'datetime' dispatches to Date (first element not int-parsable).
decimal(10,2) columns (Total, UnitPrice) store REAL; Number fuzzer with scale=10,precision=2 -> huge range, int-like perturbation on floats.
Quantity has distinct=1 (all 1); UnitPrice distinct=2 (0.99,1.99); heavy ties in original, TS fresh draws will break them.
varchar columns hold non-ASCII (Luís, François, Bjørn, Straße, ’) and embedded commas/parens/slashes; String CHARSET is ASCII-only.
PostalCode/Phone/Fax/State are text with formats ('12227-000','+55 (12) 3923-5555','SP') but declared varchar -> String fuzzer, no format template.
Small tables (MediaType 5, Employee 8, Playlist 18, Genre 25) vs Track 3503, PlaylistTrack 8715; choose_table_sizes may exceed parent sizes -> FK draws with replacement.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE columns beyond PKs; checked=False everywhere so p stays 0.2.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on BirthDate/HireDate/InvoiceDate: template from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' (or similar), range from min/max parsed dates; fresh dates uniform in that range.
Number fuzzer on all INTEGER/decimal columns: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale=0 for INTEGER, 10 for decimal(10,2)); decimal columns get values like 1e9, implausible for UnitPrice/Total.
String fuzzer on all varchar: random ASCII strings of length 0..len(varchar) plus contamination; names/emails/phones become gibberish -> FN on LIKE/format predicates.

FK columns (Album.ArtistId, Track.AlbumId/GenreId/MediaTypeId, Invoice.CustomerId, InvoiceLine.InvoiceId/TrackId, Customer.SupportRepId, PlaylistTrack.*) draw from parent's final values with replacement -> duplicates and ties appear that original lacks.
PK columns get fresh Number draws then PK-duplicate rows dropped; composite PK PlaylistTrack drops duplicate (PlaylistId,TrackId) pairs.
Small parent tables (MediaType 5, Employee 8) mean FK child columns have very few distinct values -> many ties, joins produce large result sets.
Quantity all-1 original: Number fuzzer with 1 element -> list range [1, 10^0=1] overwritten to full range, so fresh draws vary -> FP on 'quantity=1' predicates.
UnitPrice 0.99/1.99: Number fuzzer fresh draws in [-10^10,10^10] -> implausible prices, FN on price-range predicates.
NULLs: TS does not enforce NOT NULL; rows violating NOT NULL fail at insert and are skipped -> row counts shrink, some tables may end up empty.
String fuzzer on Email/Phone/PostalCode produces no '@'/format -> FN on format predicates; original ties (distinct<rows) not reproduced.
Date fuzzer p inverted: p=0.2 means element returned w.p. 0.2, fresh dates otherwise -> dates spread over 1800-2100 if <2 distinct parsed.
Self-FK Employee.ReportsTo draws from Employee's final EmployeeId list -> reports-to values may point to non-managers, breaking hierarchy predicates.
